ashley: Thinking aloud — can we add a 'cost decay' term into the policy engine so brief price spikes don't instantly flip tenants to cheaper-but-slower edges? :thinking:
mike: Love the idea. main tradeoff is stale signals causing sustained suboptimal placement. need decay window tuning.
devon: If we do this, we need split semantics: compile-time cost buckets vs runtime probe-derived short-term adjustments. runtime should be able to override but not invalidate compile decisions.
ashley: Agreed. sketching DSL idea:
```policy
when request.latency < 100ms and cost.delta < 0.2: prefer(region=us-west, weight=100)
set cost_decay = exp_decay(half_life=300s)
adjust weight -= cost_delta * cost_decay
```
sam: two practical concerns: 1) telemetry lag — decay based on observed cost might lag behind real price changes. 2) when fallback capacity is limited, decaying away from a cheap option could spike load.
natasha: For interfaces: runtime should expose only normalized 'adjustment_score' float [-1,1]. compiler/runtime agree on interpretation. That keeps kernel simple.
mike: +1. Also add an audit log entry every time runtime adjusts a compiled routing decision > threshold.
policy-sim-bot: simulation finished: 10k requests, decay half_life=300s -> 12% fewer churn events, avg latency +3ms, cost +0.7%.
ashley: Good baseline. can we run sim on bursty price pattern and capacity constrained scenario?
devon: I'll run localized sims. question: should the runtime expose probe weight (confidence) so compiler can bias future compile decisions? or keep compile isolated?
sam: exposing confidence is powerful but opens contraction: compile may oscillate if it reweights too aggressively. maybe use low-pass on compile side.
natasha: Proposal: runtime API -> {adjustment_score, confidence, decay_window_used}. compiler uses these as telemetry inputs only (no forced recompile), and we run periodic offline recompile using accumulated signals.
ashley: Sounds safe. rollout plan: feature-flag runtime decay, default off; run simulation canaries in dev and one small tenant; collect churn/latency/cost deltas.
mike: Add automatic rollback if churn rate > 2x baseline or error budget impacted.
policy-bot: created RFC-7831: "runtime-cost-decay-and-probe-interface". @ashley @devon please add design doc link.
ashley: I'll draft the RFC this afternoon. TL;DR tasks: 1) define runtime API proto 2) sim harness for bursty price patterns 3) telemetry dashboards 4) canary config.
devon: I'll own sim harness. sam can you add the telemetry dashboards? natasha to spec API schema.
sam: on it. will mock up a dashboard with churn, latency, cost, and probe confidence.
natasha: API proto draft: `message RuntimeAdjustment { float adjustment_score = 1; float confidence = 2; int32 decay_seconds = 3; }` will post in threads.
ashley: perfect. small followup: how do we reason about region constraints (data residency)? decay must never violate hard constraints.
mike: enforce hard constraints at admission — adjustments are clipped/frustrated if they conflict with policy predicates.
ashley: Cool. thanks everyone. I'll update when RFC is up.
policy-sim-bot: note: attaching sim logs -> /sims/1754219876-cost-decay-v1.tar.gz
devon: ack, starting runs now.
